findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext static credentials. EC2 user data is readable by anyone with instance metadata access (including via SSRF from the public web app) and by any principal with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking long-lived AWS credentials.
The instance defines no root_block_device or ebs_block_device with encrypted = true, so attached storage may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.
No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with an internet-facing web server, this makes credential theft via SSRF trivial.
The instance launches into a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a security group open to the world, making it directly reachable from the internet on SSH and HTTP.
Ingress on TCP port 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploit attempts.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted outbound channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control if the host is compromised.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the instance serves plain HTTP with no TLS, so traffic is transmitted in cleartext.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), so data stored on the volume is unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and specifies no KMS encryption, so the snapshot data is stored unencrypted and could be shared or copied without protection.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted.

No public access block, bucket ACL restriction, or bucket policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport is configured, leaving the flow log bucket without defence-in-depth against accidental public exposure and permitting cleartext access.
The bucket has no versioning or MFA delete and sets force_destroy = true, so audit/flow log data can be silently deleted or overwritten by an attacker covering their tracks.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, removing the network boundary between workloads and the internet.
